question: Does a resident systemd user unit around the guarded launcher serve Hermes dev sessions with fast warm reuse, within budget caps, without touching the miner?
method: scripts/serve-dev-qwen38.sh (dev launcher: same guard philosophy as the benchmark launcher, CTX 65536, no drafter by default, no qli interruption — dev coexists with the miner) + scripts/expertpin-dev.service (systemd user unit, MemoryHigh 33G / MemoryMax 36G / MemorySwapMax 16G, Restart=always backoff).
verdict: PASS — resident serving proven with warm reuse

evidence.first_query_cold: 84.4 s wall (session 20260911_165914_e79502, includes model-contact + shell tool)
evidence.second_query_warm: 15.9 s wall on the SAME server instance (no restart), exact answer 'dev-serving-check-2'
evidence.miner: qli.service stayed ACTIVE throughout (coexistence proven); GPU util 0% between queries, VRAM 17379 MiB during serving
evidence.host_after_stop: qli active, VRAM back to 2357 MiB, MemAvailable 45 GiB — night cycle unblocked

iteration: first start failed: --keep-alive 0 is not a flag in this llama-server build (usage printed); removed — slots persist across requests anyway, as the warm reuse proves
notes: Unit is NOT enabled by default (opt-in: systemctl --user enable --now expertpin-dev.service) so it cannot conflict with the 03:00 benchmark cycle or the miner schedule.
The launcher refuses to start while the host is busy (guards) and systemd retries every 30 s — self-healing start when the host frees up.
limitations: two-query warm proof, not a multi-hour soak
dev coexistence with the miner measured only at idle GPU util; a mining GPU would fail the launcher guard by design (VRAM check)
